claims.text: Engagement-driven signals can introduce popularity bias and affect predictive outcomes in crime-related social media analytics.
A fairness-aware, Pareto-based multi-objective optimization framework can be used for feature selection and Random Forest hyperparameter optimization using textual and engagement features.
NSGA-II achieved an accuracy of 0.8118 in crime classification.
NSGA-II achieved an F1-score of 0.8051 in crime classification.
NSGA-II achieved a Statistical Parity Difference (SPD) of 0.08, a Disparate Impact (DI) of 0.97, and an Equality of Opportunity Difference (EOD) of 0.06.
Removing engagement features improved standalone Accuracy and F1-score compared to retaining them.

evidence.description: NSGA-II achieved an accuracy of 0.8118 on a dataset of 32,000 crime-related tweets covering Fraud, Accident, and Murder evaluated via stratified cross-validation.
NSGA-II achieved an F1-score of 0.8051 on the 32,000 crime-related tweets dataset.
Optimization via NSGA-II resulted in an SPD of 0.08, DI of 0.97, and EOD of 0.06 when jointly minimizing fairness penalties.
Evaluation showed that removing engagement features improved standalone Accuracy and F1-score.

methodologies.name: Fairness-aware Pareto-based multi-objective optimization framework
methodologies.description: A multi-objective optimization approach using NSGA-II to jointly maximize Random Forest classification performance and minimize fairness penalties (SPD, DI, EOD) for feature selection and hyperparameter tuning.
datasets: Dataset of 32,000 crime-related tweets covering Fraud, Accident, and Murder
conditions: Comparison against PSO, ACO, and ERL

limitations.text: Engagement-driven signals introduce popularity bias and affect predictive outcomes.
Fairness evaluation was restricted to mitigating engagement-driven popularity bias across behavioral user groups rather than addressing demographic discrimination.
Retaining engagement features resulted in lower standalone accuracy and F1-score compared to completely removing them.
